place.name: Colosseum
place.summary: The 1st-century amphitheatre that once seated around 50,000 spectators — Rome’s defining monument.
place.whyVisit: Standing inside the arena shows the scale of imperial Rome better than any photo. The underground (hypogeum) and upper tiers need special tickets and sell out first.

price.includes: Standard ticket includes the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Underground / Arena levels cost extra.

hours.text: Daily from 8:30; closing time changes by season (roughly 16:30 in winter to 19:15 in summer).

place.howToGet: Metro Line B to Colosseo — the exit faces the monument.
tips: Book a timed slot on the official site; same-day tickets are rarely available in season.
Go at opening or the last slot to avoid the heat and crowds.
Bring ID — names on tickets are checked.

place.name: Roman Forum & Palatine Hill
place.summary: The ruins of ancient Rome’s political and religious heart, with the imperial palaces on the hill above.
place.whyVisit: Walking the Via Sacra past temples and triumphal arches gives context to everything else you see in Rome. The Palatine has shade, gardens and the best view over the Forum.

price.includes: Same combined ticket as the Colosseum (valid 24h, one entry per site).

hours.text: Daily from 9:00; closing time changes by season.

place.howToGet: 5 minutes’ walk from Metro Colosseo; second entrance on Via di San Gregorio.
tips: Little shade — bring water and a hat in summer.
Visit the Palatine first, then descend into the Forum.
The Terrazza del Palatino offers one of the best free-with-ticket views.

place.name: Pantheon
place.summary: A 2,000-year-old temple with the world’s largest unreinforced concrete dome and its open oculus.
place.whyVisit: The light beam from the oculus moving across the interior is unforgettable, and the visit takes only 20–30 minutes — easy to fit into any walk.

price.includes: Entry to the interior. Free for under-18s and on some religious services.

hours.text: Daily roughly 9:00–19:00; access can change during masses.

place.howToGet: 10 minutes’ walk from Piazza Navona; buses to Corso Rinascimento or Largo di Torre Argentina.
tips: Book online to skip the ticket queue.
Come back to the square at night when it is lit and lively.

place.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
place.summary: One of the world’s great art collections, ending in Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel ceiling.
place.whyVisit: Raphael Rooms, the Gallery of Maps and the Sistine Chapel in a single route. Plan at least three hours and pace yourself.

price.includes: Museum route including the Sistine Chapel. Online booking adds a reservation fee.

hours.text: Mon–Sat, typically 8:00–19:00 (last entry earlier). Closed most Sundays except the last Sunday of the month.

place.howToGet: Metro Line A to Ottaviano or Cipro, then 5–10 minutes’ walk.
tips: Shoulders and knees must be covered.
Photography is not allowed in the Sistine Chapel.
Friday evening openings (seasonal) are calmer.

place.name: St. Peter’s Basilica & Dome
place.summary: The largest church in the world, with Michelangelo’s Pietà and a climbable dome.
place.whyVisit: Entry to the basilica is free; the dome climb (551 steps, or lift + 320 steps) rewards you with the best panorama in Rome.

price.includes: Basilica free. Dome climb paid (stairs or lift option).

hours.text: Basilica usually from 7:00 to 18:00–19:00; dome closes earlier.

place.howToGet: Metro Line A to Ottaviano, then 10 minutes’ walk down Via di Porta Angelica.
tips: Security queue is shortest before 8:00.
Dress code is enforced (covered shoulders and knees).

place.name: Trevi Fountain
place.summary: The baroque fountain where visitors toss a coin to guarantee a return to Rome.
place.whyVisit: It is genuinely spectacular, but the experience depends on timing — early morning or late night is a completely different place.

price.includes: The square is free. The city has introduced managed access/fee for the area next to the basin — check before you go.

hours.text: Square open 24h; managed basin access has set hours.

place.howToGet: 10 minutes’ walk from Metro Barberini or Spagna.
tips: Visit before 8:00 for photos without crowds.
Throw the coin with your right hand over your left shoulder.

place.name: Galleria Borghese
place.summary: Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings in an intimate villa — entry by 2-hour timed slot only.
place.whyVisit: Bernini’s Apollo and Daphne seen up close is one of Rome’s great moments. Limited numbers keep it calm.

price.includes: Timed 2-hour entry; reservation mandatory, booking fee applies.

hours.text: Tue–Sun 9:00–19:00 in timed slots; closed Mondays.

place.howToGet: Bus 910 or 61 to Pinciana/Museo Borghese, or a 20-minute park walk from Metro Spagna.
tips: Book weeks ahead in high season.
Combine with a walk in Villa Borghese park and the Pincio terrace.

media.credit: José Luiz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
media.alt: The exterior facade of Galleria Borghese in Rome.
media.caption: Galleria Borghese exterior, photographed in 2015.

place.name: Spanish Steps & Piazza di Spagna
place.summary: 135 baroque steps linking Piazza di Spagna with Trinità dei Monti church.
place.whyVisit: The heart of the elegant Tridente — combine with Via Condotti shopping and the view from the top.
place.howToGet: Metro Line A to Spagna.
tips: Sitting on the steps is prohibited and fined.
Walk up to Trinità dei Monti for the view down Via Condotti.

place.name: Castel Sant’Angelo
place.summary: Hadrian’s mausoleum turned papal fortress, with a rooftop terrace over the Tiber.
place.whyVisit: The terrace view toward St. Peter’s is superb at sunset, and the Ponte Sant’Angelo angels make the approach memorable.
place.howToGet: Metro Line A to Lepanto, or 10 minutes’ walk from Piazza Navona across Ponte Sant’Angelo.
tips: The café on the upper level has one of the best-value views in Rome.

place.name: Trastevere evening stroll
place.address: Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere
place.summary: Ivy-covered lanes, a 12th-century mosaic church and Rome’s liveliest evening atmosphere.
place.whyVisit: Best as a slow evening: golden-hour walk, dinner in a trattoria, then a drink on Piazza Trilussa.
place.howToGet: Tram 8 from Largo Argentina to Belli or Trastevere/Mastai; or walk across Ponte Sisto.
tips: Santa Maria in Trastevere’s mosaics are free to see.
Restaurants on the main squares cost more — go one street back.

place.name: Capitoline Museums
place.summary: The world’s oldest public museum, on Michelangelo’s piazza, home of the Capitoline Wolf.
place.whyVisit: Far calmer than the Vatican, with the original Marcus Aurelius statue and a terrace over the Forum.
place.howToGet: 5 minutes’ walk from Piazza Venezia; buses to Piazza Venezia.
tips: The Tabularium gallery offers a free-with-ticket Forum view.

media.credit: Jean-Pol GRANDMONT · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

place.name: Baths of Caracalla
place.summary: Vast 3rd-century bath complex with towering walls and mosaic floors; summer opera venue.
place.whyVisit: Massive, atmospheric and rarely crowded — a quieter alternative to the Forum.
place.howToGet: Metro Line B to Circo Massimo, then 7 minutes’ walk.
tips: Check the Caracalla Festival programme for open-air opera in summer.

media.credit: Ethan Doyle White · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

place.name: Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina
place.summary: Deli-restaurant famous for carbonara, cured meats and a serious wine list.
place.whyVisit: One of the most reliable places for the Roman classics done with exceptional ingredients.

price.includes: Pasta, main or cheese plate, glass of wine.

place.howToGet: 3 minutes’ walk from Campo de’ Fiori.
tips: Reserve several days ahead, especially for dinner.
Ask for the counter if you’re two.

place.name: Da Enzo al 29
place.summary: Tiny family trattoria for cacio e pepe, amatriciana and Roman artichokes.
place.whyVisit: Authentic, generous and good value — the kind of place locals queue for.

hours.text: Mon–Sat lunch and dinner; usually closed Sunday.

place.howToGet: Tram 8 to Belli, then 5 minutes’ walk.
tips: Arrive 15 minutes before opening or expect to queue.
Order the tiramisù early — it sells out.

place.name: Armando al Pantheon
place.summary: Family-run since 1961, steps from the Pantheon — classic Roman cooking.
place.whyVisit: Rare example of an excellent, honest restaurant right next to a major monument.

hours.text: Mon–Sat lunch and dinner; closed Sunday.

place.howToGet: 1 minute from the Pantheon.
tips: Book online — walk-ins are rarely possible.

place.name: Pizzarium Bonci
place.summary: Gabriele Bonci’s celebrated pizza by the slice with creative toppings.
place.whyVisit: A perfect fast lunch after the Vatican Museums.

hours.text: Daily, late morning to late evening.

place.howToGet: Opposite Metro Cipro (Line A).
tips: Standing only — take it to the benches outside.
Point at 3–4 different slices to share.

place.name: Antico Forno Roscioli
place.summary: Historic bakery for pizza bianca, pizza rossa and Roman pastries.
place.whyVisit: Cheap, fast and outstanding — Rome’s street-food breakfast or snack.

hours.text: Mon–Sat from early morning; Sunday reduced.

place.howToGet: 2 minutes from Campo de’ Fiori.
tips: Take a number at the counter.

media.caption: The bakery sign photographed in 2012.
media.changes: Resized and converted to WebP. Cards may display a crop.

place.name: Giolitti
place.summary: Gelateria open since 1900, a short walk from the Pantheon.
place.whyVisit: A classic Roman ritual — pay first at the till, then order at the counter.
place.howToGet: 4 minutes’ walk from the Pantheon.
tips: Ask for panna (whipped cream) on top — usually free.

media.credit: Chino at en.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

place.name: Sant’Eustachio Il Caffè
place.summary: Legendary espresso bar roasting its own beans since 1938.
place.whyVisit: Try the Gran Caffè, standing at the bar like a Roman. Bags of beans make a good gift.

hours.text: Daily, early morning to late evening.

place.howToGet: 2 minutes from the Pantheon.
tips: Coffee at the bar is cheaper than at a table.
Say “amaro” if you want it without sugar — it comes sweetened by default.

place.name: Trapizzino Trastevere
place.summary: Pizza-dough pockets filled with Roman stews like chicken cacciatora or oxtail.
place.whyVisit: Quick, cheap and very Roman — ideal before a night out in Trastevere.
place.howToGet: At the Trastevere end of Ponte Sisto.
tips: Pair with a supplì (fried rice ball).

place.name: Freni e Frizioni
place.summary: Former garage turned cocktail bar with a busy aperitivo buffet.
place.whyVisit: The young-Roman aperitivo scene — drinks spill out onto the piazza.

price.includes: Aperitivo snacks with a drink in early evening.

place.howToGet: Across Ponte Sisto, first left.
tips: Arrive around 19:00 for aperitivo.

place.name: Drink Kong
place.address: Piazza di San Martino ai Monti 8
place.summary: Neon-lit, Japanese-inspired cocktail bar regularly in international best-bar lists.
place.whyVisit: For a special-occasion cocktail in a design-forward setting.
place.howToGet: 8 minutes’ walk from Metro Vittorio Emanuele or Cavour.
tips: Book a table online for weekends.

place.name: Bar del Fico
place.summary: Lively bar under a fig tree behind Piazza Navona; locals play chess outside.
place.whyVisit: Easy, central spot for an evening drink after walking the historic centre.
place.howToGet: 3 minutes west of Piazza Navona.
tips: Terrace tables fill around 20:00.

place.name: Campo de’ Fiori market
place.summary: Morning open-air market with produce, spices, pasta and edible souvenirs.
place.whyVisit: Lively and photogenic. Some stalls target tourists, so compare prices.

price.includes: Dried pasta, spice mixes, limoncello miniatures.

place.howToGet: 5 minutes south of Piazza Navona.
tips: Compare prices between stalls — packaged “Roman spice” sets vary a lot.
Pair with Antico Forno Roscioli nearby.

place.name: Mercato di Testaccio
place.summary: Modern covered market where Romans shop — produce, cheese, and great street-food stalls.
place.whyVisit: More local and better value than Campo de’ Fiori, plus excellent lunch counters.
place.howToGet: Metro Line B to Piramide, then 10 minutes’ walk.
tips: Ask cheese stalls to vacuum-pack for travel.

media.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Joris assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

place.name: Porta Portese Sunday market
place.address: Via Portuense / Piazza di Porta Portese
place.summary: Rome’s huge Sunday flea market: vintage, antiques, clothes and bric-à-brac.
place.whyVisit: Bargain hunting and people-watching; arrive early for the best finds.
place.howToGet: Tram 8 to Ippolito Nievo or Trastevere/Ministero Istruzione.
tips: Cash only at most stalls; keep valuables secure.
Bargaining is expected.

media.credit: Gustavo La Pizza · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

place.name: Via dei Condotti & Tridente
place.summary: Rome’s luxury shopping street running down from the Spanish Steps.
place.whyVisit: Flagships of the big Italian houses plus Antico Caffè Greco (1760).
place.howToGet: Metro Line A to Spagna.
tips: Non-EU residents can claim VAT refunds on purchases above the minimum — ask for the tax-free form.

place.name: Castel Romano Designer Outlet
place.address: Via del Ponte di Piscina Cupa 64
place.summary: Large designer outlet south of the city with Italian and international brands.
place.whyVisit: Discounts on previous-season fashion — worth it if shopping is a priority.

price.includes: Shuttle bus from central Rome is paid separately.

place.howToGet: Dedicated shuttle from Termini area (paid), or car/taxi.
tips: Plan half a day including the transfer.

place.name: Volpetti
place.summary: Famous gourmet deli: cheeses, cured meats, truffle products, olive oil.
place.whyVisit: High-quality edible gifts, vacuum-packed for travel on request.
place.howToGet: Metro Line B to Piramide, then 5 minutes’ walk.
tips: Ask for tastings before buying.
Check your home country’s customs rules for meat and dairy.

place.name: Antica Caciara Trasteverina
place.address: Via di San Francesco a Ripa 140
place.summary: Old-school cheese shop known for pecorino romano and ricotta.
place.whyVisit: Pecorino is the key ingredient of carbonara and cacio e pepe — a perfect edible souvenir.
place.howToGet: Tram 8 to Trastevere/Mastai, 3 minutes’ walk.
tips: Ask for vacuum packing.

place.name: Ai Monasteri
place.summary: Historic shop selling products made in Italian monasteries: liqueurs, honey, soaps, creams.
place.whyVisit: Unusual, beautifully packaged gifts you won’t find in souvenir stalls.

hours.text: Mon–Sat with midday break; check before visiting.

place.howToGet: 2 minutes from Piazza Navona.
tips: Herbal soaps and honey travel well in hand luggage.

place.name: Rinascente · Via del Tritone
place.summary: Fashion, beauty, design and gourmet shopping near the Trevi Fountain.
place.whyVisit: Compare several kinds of gifts in one department store, then explore the aqueduct remains in the building.

hours.text: Check the official store page for current hours and holiday openings.

place.howToGet: Walk from the Trevi Fountain or approach from Barberini. Entrance pin is for orientation.
tips: Choose a budget before browsing; stock and prices vary by brand.
Check the receipt and return terms before paying.

place.name: Feltrinelli · Largo Argentina
place.summary: A central bookshop for a literary stop and a gift to read on the journey home.
place.whyVisit: Browse books near Largo Argentina. Ask staff about the language and edition you need before choosing a gift.
place.howToGet: Approach from Largo di Torre Argentina; use the numbered address to find the entrance.
tips: Confirm the book language before buying.
Check the official page for events and holiday hours.

place.name: Castroni · Cola di Rienzo
place.summary: Coffee, Italian pantry products, tea and sweets in the Prati shopping district.
place.whyVisit: Build a small edible gift around coffee or packaged pantry products. Check the origin label if you want something specifically Italian.

hours.text: Confirm current hours with the Cola di Rienzo branch before visiting.

place.howToGet: Find the shop on Via Cola di Rienzo in Prati; the address identifies this branch.
tips: Ask for a grind suitable for the recipient’s coffee maker.
Check package weight, ingredients and expiry date.

place.name: Fabriano Boutique · Babuino
place.summary: A paper and stationery stop for a travel notebook or a gift for someone who loves writing.
place.whyVisit: Choose a journal for your own journey or explore paper gifts away from the usual souvenir stalls.

hours.text: Daily 10:00–20:00 in the official locator. Holiday exceptions may apply.

place.howToGet: Walk along Via del Babuino between Piazza del Popolo and the Spanish Steps. Pin is approximate.
tips: Check paper size and ruling before choosing a notebook.
Confirm the selection and current opening hours with the boutique.

place.name: Momonì · Babuino
place.summary: A fashion boutique on Via del Babuino for a focused shopping stop.
place.whyVisit: Explore one boutique rather than an entire department store; combine it with a walk through the Tridente.

hours.text: Daily 10:30–19:30 in the official locator. Confirm holiday hours.

place.howToGet: Walk along Via del Babuino from Piazza del Popolo or Spagna. Pin is approximate.
tips: Try the fit and confirm the return policy.
Check availability with the shop if you need a particular size.

place.name: Hotel Artemide
place.summary: Art Nouveau 4-star hotel with a rooftop terrace, well-placed between Termini and the centre.
place.whyVisit: Reliable comfort and transport links at a fair mid-range price.
place.howToGet: Metro Line A to Repubblica, 3 minutes’ walk.
tips: Request a quieter room away from Via Nazionale.

place.name: Hotel de Russie
place.summary: Rocco Forte luxury hotel with a famous terraced “secret garden” near Piazza del Popolo.
place.whyVisit: Top-tier service and a calm garden in the most elegant part of town.
place.howToGet: Metro Line A to Flaminio, 3 minutes’ walk.
tips: Even if not staying, the Stravinskij Bar is open to visitors.

place.name: Hotel Santa Maria
place.summary: Former cloister with an orange-tree courtyard in the heart of Trastevere.
place.whyVisit: Quiet base in Rome’s most charming evening neighbourhood.
place.howToGet: Tram 8 to Trastevere/Mastai, 5 minutes’ walk.
tips: Bikes are often available for guests.

media.credit: György Farkas from Budapest, Hungary · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

place.name: Hotel Raphael
place.summary: Ivy-covered hotel next to Piazza Navona with a panoramic rooftop terrace.
place.whyVisit: Unbeatable location for walking the historic centre.
place.howToGet: 1 minute from Piazza Navona.
tips: Rooftop bar is open to non-guests — book for sunset.

place.name: The Beehive
place.summary: Eco-minded, independently run budget hotel/hostel near Termini with a garden.
place.whyVisit: Friendly, clean and good value — a safe choice for budget travellers.
place.howToGet: 4 minutes from Termini station.
tips: Private rooms sell out first.

place.name: Generator Rome
place.summary: Design hostel with private rooms and dorms, bar and terrace.
place.whyVisit: Social atmosphere and low prices, 10 minutes from Termini.
place.howToGet: Metro Line A to Vittorio Emanuele, 5 minutes’ walk.
tips: Area is lively at night — choose upper floors for quiet.

place.name: Leonardo Express (Fiumicino ⇄ Termini)
place.summary: Non-stop train between Fiumicino Airport (FCO) and Termini, about 32 minutes.
place.whyVisit: The fastest predictable link from FCO to the centre.
place.howToGet: At FCO follow “Treni / Trains” signs; in Rome departs from Termini platforms 23–24.
tips: Regional FL1 trains are cheaper and stop at Trastevere/Ostiense.
Validate paper tickets before boarding.

place.name: Fixed-fare taxi from Fiumicino
place.summary: Licensed white Rome taxis charge a fixed fare from FCO to inside the Aurelian Walls.
place.whyVisit: Door-to-door, good value for 3–4 people or with luggage.

price.includes: Up to 4 passengers with luggage, to destinations inside the Aurelian Walls.

place.howToGet: Use only the official taxi rank outside arrivals.
tips: Ignore drivers soliciting inside the terminal.
Confirm the fixed fare before departing.

place.name: Ciampino Airport bus
place.summary: Shuttle buses link low-cost-airline hub Ciampino (CIA) with Termini in ~40 minutes.
place.whyVisit: Cheapest way into the city from CIA.
place.howToGet: Bus stops outside arrivals; Termini stop on Via Giolitti.
tips: Fixed taxi fare from Ciampino to the centre also applies.

media.credit: Hayden Soloviev · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

place.name: Metro, buses & trams (ATAC)
place.summary: Three metro lines plus buses and trams. One ticket (BIT) is valid 100 minutes.
place.whyVisit: Contactless bank cards can be tapped at metro gates — no need to buy paper tickets.
place.howToGet: Main interchange at Termini (Lines A & B).
tips: Beware of pickpockets on Line A and bus 64.
Most of the centre is easiest on foot.

place.name: Walking route: Pantheon → Navona → Campo de’ Fiori
place.summary: A 1.5 km, mostly flat loop through the historic centre’s most beautiful squares.
place.whyVisit: Shows how close Rome’s highlights are — perfect for a light day.
place.howToGet: Start at the Pantheon; finish at Campo de’ Fiori.
tips: Allow 1–2 hours with stops; add gelato at Giolitti.
